title: A 3,800-Year-Old Sealed Letter Was Read Without Opening It
mediaSource: Assyrian cuneiform sealed clay envelope CT scan Kanesh letter

scenes.title: They read a sealed letter without breaking it
scenes.narration: Ancient Assyrian clay letters were often wrapped in clay envelopes that had to be broken open. This time, researchers read the message without destroying the envelope.

scenes.title: A 3,800-year-old message appeared
scenes.narration: Using non-destructive scanning, researchers reconstructed writing hidden inside sealed tablets from the ancient city of Kanesh in Türkiye.

scenes.title: One letter contained a woman's complaint
scenes.narration: One message was sent by a woman named Anna-anna to her husband. She described her frustration while trying to recover silver that someone owed him.

scenes.title: Breaking the envelope destroys evidence
scenes.narration: Clay envelopes can preserve seals and transaction marks, so opening them can erase valuable archaeological information.

scenes.title: Now closed documents can stay intact
scenes.narration: The new imaging approach can reveal hidden writing while preserving the artifact, making it useful for other sealed clay documents.

scenes.title: A private conversation survived for 3,800 years
scenes.narration: Inside an unopened clay envelope, an ordinary story about family and money survived. Modern imaging has given that ancient voice a way out.
